newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-EIB swoops for HK dollars.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-EIB swoops for HK dollars.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) swooped on the Hong Kong market for the second time in two months with a HK$500 million fixed-rate bond issue on Tuesday.
The seven-year issue carried a quarterly 7.27 percent coupon, was issued at 100.20, and paid a yield to investors of 7.432 percent, sole arranger Societe Generale Asia told Reuters.
It was launched at a spread of 34 basis points over Exchange Fund notes.
Bankers said the EIB deal had "rarity" value because it had previously favoured five-year issues, although some thought pricing was a little tight.
"It's not desperately attractive, but it's not too bad," said one banker who took some of the EIB seven-year paper.
In April, an EIB HK$1.0 billion 10-year fixed-rate bond went at a spread of 33 basis points over Exchange Fund notes, and carried a 7.58 percent coupon.
That deal was eligible for the liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) operated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), making it more attractive to investors.
But at HK$500 million, Tuesday's EIB fixed-rate bond was too small to qualify for the LAF.
Comparisons with earlier EIB Hong Kong bond issues, even five-year deals, show how yields are falling.
In September, a HK$1 billion EIB five-year bond issue paid an annual re-offer yield of 7.69 percent annually.
And a HK$500 million five-year bond issue by the EIB in June last year was priced to yield 7.68 percent annually.
Bankers said they were seeing a steady flow of corporates seeking refinancing to take advantage of lower interest rates.
"Every company in town right now is looking at this chance to lock in low rates," one banker with a U.S. bank said.
Blue chip property company Hang Lung Development Co Ltd said this week that it had cut its funding costs by HK$10 million to HK$20 million a year through refinancing.
HSBC Investment Bank Asia and Chase Manhattan Asia are now inviting banks to join the HK$10 billion five-year loan for Hutchison Whampoa Ltd facility as underwriters.
A revolving credit for the first year, it converts to a term loan, and pays a margin of 39 basis points over the one-, two- and three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
The planned HK$7 billion to HK$8 billion loan facility being planned for a development at Tseung Kwan O in Hong Kong's New Territories is finding favour with banks, bankers said.
One banker said every major bank in town was lining up for the loan, by a joint venture between Swire Properties Ltd and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd.
Siam Commercial Bank's US$100 million floating rate certificate of deposit (FRCD) issue has been allotted, bookrunner BA Asia said on Tuesday.
Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd's floating-rate note issue has been increasd to US$81 million from US$70 million, bankers said.
The dual-tranche FRCD from First Pacific Bank, a unit of FPB Bank Holding Co, has been lifted to the equivalent of about HK$700 million, from HK$500 million, bankers said.
Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd said it was the right time to launch a Samurai bond, and would launch its three-year Yen 30 billion Samurai next month.
